title: Empirical Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be finite, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. Given $m$ labeled examples $(x_j,y_j)$ in $\{−1,1\}^n\times\{−1,1\}$, the empirical Fourier coefficient on $S$ is $\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=0}^{m-1} y_j\prod_{i\in S}(x_j)_i$, with the expression understood as the rational sum divided by $m$.
hypotheses_covered: The sample is a function from the $m$ sample indices to labeled examples in $\{−1,1\}^n\times\{−1,1\}$
